review_candidates.description: Job Description Join the HJF Team! HJF is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow whois responsible for initiating and carrying out research projects in collaboration with a research team. The Postdoctoral Research fellow will be working on a National Science Foundation (NSF) funded project that aims to build the first integrated phylogenomic, morphological, and ecological framework of the entire Anopheline mosquito subfamily. Mosquitoes are the deadliest animals on Earth, and anopheline mosquitoes alone transmit the malaria parasites responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths every year. Their ranges are shifting in unpredictable ways under climate and land-use change, yet fewer than 75 of the nearly 500 known Anopheline species have ever been tested for their ability to transmit human pathogens; and most lack even a basic evolutionary or ecological framework. The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will lead genomic assembly and phylogenomic inference, contribute to 3D morphometric trait extraction and environmental niche modeling, and co-lead peer-reviewed manuscripts across multiple aims. This is an unusually broad, integrative opportunity for a scientist who wants to work at the intersection of phylogenomics, functional morphology, ecology, and public health entomology, with the training, publications, and network to launch an independent research career. The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals. Responsibilities Lead sample preparation, DNA extraction, and library preparation from museum and contemporary specimens. Perform whole-genome shotgun, reduced-representation, and long-read sequencing workflows, adapting protocols for archival and fresh material. Assemble genomes and recover single-copy nuclear orthologs in a reference-guided framework across specimens. Perform locus alignment, gene-tree and species-tree inference, and time calibration using fossil priors. Quantify gene-tree discordance and detect introgression. Delimit cryptic species and refine complex boundaries using integrated genomic evidence. Contribute to micro-CT scanning to downstream 3D segmentation of thoracic musculature and wing architecture. Compute Relative Dispersal Capacity (RDC) and related biomechanical traits from micro-CT-derived morphology. Build and refine environmental niche hypervolumes, remotely sensed land cover, and curated occurrence data. Familiarity with 3D morphometrics, CT segmentation, or biomechanical modeling. Demonstrate knowledge of species distribution modeling, GIS, or remote sensing. Interest or background in One-Health, vector biology, or bioinformatics. Experience mentoring students and contributing to an inclusive, collaborative team environment. A track record of first-author peer-reviewed publications appropriate to career stage. Strong written and oral communication skills. Demonstrated ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues across. Ability to obtain and maintain a T1 Public Trust background check.
